name: Onychomatricoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological diagnostic criteria for Onychomatricoma

criteria.description: Presence of a thickened, yellowish, and overcurved nail plate with longitudinal bands
Histological identification of fibroepithelial tumor with digitations and epithelial invaginations in the nail matrix
Ultrasound or MRI showing a well-defined tumor in the nail matrix with finger-like projections
Extraction of nail plate revealing multiple filiform projections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical features plus histopathological confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; imaging can aid in preoperative assessment.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Longitudinal yellow bands on nail plate
searchTerms: yellow bands running lengthwise on nails

pathognomonic.symptomName: Filiform projections visible after nail plate removal

common.symptomName: Splinter hemorrhages under the nail plate

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or tenderness of the affected digit
searchTerms: slight discomfort in finger or toe

occasional.symptomName: Onycholysis (separation of nail plate from nail bed)

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of the nail fold
Nail plate fragility leading to spontaneous nail loss

imaging: Ultrasound showing hypoechoic tumor with finger-like projections in the nail matrix
MRI demonstrating well-defined lesion with digitations in the nail matrix
other: Histopathology revealing fibroepithelial tumor with epithelial invaginations and stromal digitations
Nail plate extraction showing multiple filiform projections

distinguishingFeatures: Fungal infection confirmed by microscopy or culture
Lack of filiform projections on nail plate extraction
Hard subungual mass rather than fibroepithelial tumor
Absence of characteristic nail plate changes seen in onychomatricoma
Severe localized pain, especially with cold exposure
MRI showing vascular tumor distinct from nail matrix fibroepithelial tumor
No characteristic nail plate thickening or filiform projections

redFlags: Persistent pain unresponsive to conservative treatment
Signs suggestive of malignant transformation such as ulceration or bleeding
references: Baran R, Kint A. Onychomatricoma: a new tumor of the nail matrix. J Am Acad Dermatol. 1992.
Richert B, et al. Onychomatricoma: clinical, histopathological and immunohistochemical study of 30 cases. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2012.
